chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Zarih al-Muharibi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever dies and has not performed the Hajj of Islam, and was not prevented from that he was not prevented by a need that crushes him, or an illness in which he cannot endure the Hajj, or a ruler who prevents him, so let him die as a Jew or a Christian.

key_terms.مَرَضٌ لَا يُطِيقُ فِيهِ الْحَجَّ: Illness preventing the endurance of Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who dies without performing Hajj if they were able to do so?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the urgency of Hajj, distinguishing between valid excuses and mere negligence. The phrase 'let him die as a Jew or a Christian' is interpreted by Shia scholars not as apostasy, but as a metaphor for the spiritual deficiency of one who neglects a fundamental pillar of Islam while possessing the capacity to perform it. This highlights the high status of Hajj as a decisive marker of Islamic identity and obedience.
